comments.author: mmh0000
comments.story: US Government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5
comments.text: That video makes a lot of claims that sound reasonable, but doesn't provide data to back it up. For example, in the first 30 seconds, he says that at the beginning of the Iran War, AI was used to strike 900 targets in 12 hours. Which he calls "unprecedented" but then never backs up. For context, in the 1991 Gulf War "Operation Desert Storm" the U.S. struck about 1500 targets[1][2][3] in 12 hours. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO] [3] [LINK] -

comments.author: trevorishere
comments.why: Visual illustration of the 76-aircraft strike package.
comments.text: It's an airshow maneuver. Speed is life. USAF (and presumably other AF's) send out 2 to 4 ship (or if we look at Desert Storm, over 70 ships). If you "stall" or perform this maneuver, whomever is behind you might overshoot, but his or her buddy will nab you. Check out Stroke 3. This is an F-16 strike on an oil facility in Iraq. Stroke 3 avoided six Iraq (Russian-made) SAMs /without/ deploying any counter measures. Simply amazing to listen to. [LINK] And here's a visual illustration of the entire strike package that went out. 76 aircraft as part of Package Q. [VIDEO] Fun (?) fact -- the first strike in Desert Storm was performed by eight Apache attack helicopters with two Pave Low helicopters leading them at NAP of the earth level at nighttime.
